caption: I earn R48 200 and have about R2 000 left. Does a bigger salary just mean a bigger version of the same problem?

slides.title:
How I spend my R48 200
p/m salary
and still run short
Living in Umhlanga
slides.body:
Male, 37
Married, three kids (9, 7 and 2)
Job: Sales manager, car dealership
Net salary: R48 200 p/m

slides.title: Bond repayment
slides.body: We stretched for the estate. The bond is the reason I still say yes to overtime.

slides.title: School fees
slides.includes: Two at a private school, one at a crèche
slides.body: The fees went up 9% in January. I read it as a challenge.

slides.title: Two cars
slides.body: I need one for work. My wife needs one for the school run. Nobody likes the sum.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Five people, the kids' lunch boxes, Woolies
slides.body: I tried the cheaper shop once. The kids found out.

slides.title: Medical aid
slides.includes: Family plan, with the in-hospital extras
slides.body: The one thing I won't touch. My younger brother's hospital bill taught me that.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Petrol R2 400, Electricity R2 100, Fibre & phones R1 100, Golf club R650, Funeral policies R420, Black tax R800
slides.body: The golf club is the number I'm least proud of. I play once a month.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R48 200. A bigger salary didn't make this section any simpler. It just moved the zeroes.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded my statements to Beyond Horizon and it sorted every transaction for me.

The fixed costs were 80% of my pay before I'd bought a single extra thing.

No bank login needed.
